761	that sees the lack of the poor and feels his pain,

762	but rather from the word of HaShem, who created the order of the world,

763	in which there are poor and rich. As we said, "gomel dalim":

764	the Holy One, blessed be He, created in the world a reality

765	in which there are poor people. How do you look at this?

766	Do you see it as though the Holy One, blessed be He, isn't

767	in the world, and so I'm dealing with a flaw here

768	in nature, in the cosmos? And so you give

769	them tzedakah with some feeling of pity

770	for this poor wretch. You don't look at them, waiting for them

771	to just pass by.

772	Or do you understand that the Holy One, blessed be He, is in the world? Gomel

773	dalim. The poor fill a known role in the world.

774	Without them the world would lack balance and would not be

775	whole, and would not reach the supreme goal that its Creator,

776	blessed be He, set before it. And it turns out that the poor,

777	who complete the balance of the world through their poverty,

778	are in effect paid for this, and they come for their due in justice.

779	Gemul, "reward": this is their reward. Giving to the poor. The gimel

780	is attached to the dalet, a hint from the Torah, from

781	the Sages, to say that a person gives the poor what

782	is due to them as a reward, and not just some

783	favor. Then the Gemara continues and says: what is the simple meaning

784	of the verse? The gimel regarding the dalet: in the graphic form of the gimel

785	it is as if there is a leg that, so to speak, runs after

786	the dalet. What do the Sages learn from this? That it is the way of one who bestows

787	kindness to run after the poor.

788	One who bestows kindness, who has already reached his highest level,

789	recognizes that the tzedakah he gives doesn't come only from

790	his instinct, that he cannot bear to see the suffering

791	of the poor, so that there is room for it only when

792	the poor happen to come before him and their pain is placed

793	before him. But one who bestows kindness,

794	who knows the supreme role of tzedakah, the holy happiness

795	that the community and the individual gain through

796	tzedakah, will always run after

797	tzedakah and kindness, and his way will always be to find a place

798	to expand the works of kindness. You understand, once again,
